name: lexbor-917742f8-blind30
instr:
# lexbor: diagnosing injected behaviour regressions without a test suite

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

A program built on this code takes in markup and the presentation rules that travel with it, builds a tree, answers questions about that tree, changes it, and writes it back out again. It now gets a long list of those things wrong. The inputs did not change and the calling programs did not change, yet material that used to be taken in is now rejected, answers that used to be right now come back wrong, and in several places work that used to finish stops with an error instead.

Getting material in is where it starts. A file carrying a block of presentation text inside its markup ends in a memory allocation failure instead of a tree, and it does so for such a block whether or not it sits in the ordinary markup namespace. A type declaration at the head of a file whose system keyword is followed by something other than a quoted identifier comes back without the flag that forces the old compatibility mode. Markup containing characters spelled out in four bytes draws spurious complaints about those characters, the value rebuilt from the four bytes being wrong. Handing in a run of presentation declarations on their own swallows the opening piece of every value, so what comes back holds the wrong text or the whole run is refused outright. Chopping such text into its pieces loses a character at the end of each aside written between markers, so whatever
